note: Flag Anonymous extends the Flag module: for a flag it is enabled on, anonymous users who lack permission to flag see a configurable '@login or @register to use this flag' CTA (optionally in a modal) instead of the flag link, and are auto-flagged after they authenticate. No configure route, no permissions, no plugins, no drush. Its only state is third-party settings on each Flag config entity (flag.flag.<id>.third_party.flag_anon, key 'enabled' plus message/labels/popup options). It works by decorating the flag.link_builder service with FlagAnonLinkBuilder (via FlagAnonServiceProvider). Medium/hard cases are grounded in a real Flag config entity 'flaganon_eval' created against the Article bundle; setup/reset build it with drush php:eval and cleanup deletes it, so the shared site is left with no such flag.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal flag_anon module, there is no dedicated settings page. Where do you turn on the anonymous 'login/register to use this flag' behavior for a given flag, and where is that setting stored?
evals.expected_output: You enable it per flag in the 'Anonymous settings' section of the flag's edit form (there is no configure route). It is stored as third-party settings on the flag config entity: flag.flag.<id>.third_party.flag_anon, with the master switch key 'enabled'.

evals.prompt: In flag_anon's anonymous message, what do the @login and @register placeholders become, and how would I add my own custom placeholder to that message?
evals.expected_output: @login and @register are replaced with rendered links to the user login and registration forms. Add custom placeholders by implementing hook_flag_anon_message_placeholders_alter(&$placeholders, $flag, $entity) and adding a key like $placeholders['@help'] = ...->toString().

evals.prompt: I enabled flag_anon 'Anonymous settings' on a flag, but anonymous visitors still see the normal flag link instead of the login/register message. What permission-related precondition am I missing, and how does flag_anon replace the link technically?
evals.expected_output: The anonymous role must NOT have flag/unflag permission for that flag; the CTA only appears when the anonymous user lacks access (build() checks actionAccess). Technically flag_anon decorates the flag.link_builder service with FlagAnonLinkBuilder, which returns the flag_anon_message render array instead of the link.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site a flag has Flag Anonymous enabled. Inspect the live flag configuration and tell me which flag it is (machine id) and what message anonymous users are shown.
evals.expected_output: The flag flaganon_eval has third_party_settings.flag_anon.enabled = 1 and message '@login or @register to save this to your favorites'.

evals.prompt: This site has a Flag with machine id 'flaganon_eval' (on Article nodes) but Flag Anonymous is not turned on for it. Use the flag_anon module to enable the anonymous login/register behavior on that flag, applying the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set the flaganon_eval flag's third-party setting flag_anon.enabled to a truthy value (e.g. $flag->setThirdPartySetting('flag_anon','enabled',1); $flag->save(); or tick 'Show this flag to anonymous users...' in the flag's Anonymous settings and save).
